reviewed_version: W1-30.md as materially rewritten by W1-30-VIS-REVIEW, 2026-08-14
verdict: MATERIAL EDIT, not approval. The rewrite's central judgement is correct and its architecture is sound: statistics demoted to a regression tripwire, minimum-over-shots, mandatory motion and orbit gates, an unseen census sample, a planted tell, and a decomposition by file ownership. But the instrument placed on top of that machinery half-repeats the failure the rewrite exists to cure. Six material defects found and repaired as amendments R1-R6 in the parent, plus a new child W1-30K.
central_finding: The rewrite made the primary quality signal a fresh naive 1-10 'Craft' score against 'anchored comparison plates placed at known ladder positions', naming no instrument by path. That is (a) a second implementation of RI-VIS06 Protocol A, which is rule 10 - the rule that gave this project a good detection model and a broken one at once; (b) justified by a premise that has been false since 2026-08-06, namely that legal paired modern pixels do not exist - corpus/70-visual/refs/modern/ now holds 131 files across seven profile folders, including 43 exterior_daylight frames at 1920x1080 with 39 pixel_metrics_valid; and (c) unanchored at its own load-bearing rung, because every modern plate is a shipped AAA frame near the top of the ladder and nothing in the corpus sits at 7, so the absolute 'Craft >= 7.0' rows in W1-30D, W1-30E and W1-30G are opinions wearing numbers. Repaired by binding the human read to RI-VIS06 Protocol A against profile-matched plates, with its native ladder mapping and its caps. Note the cap that decides the tree: RI-VIS06 caps FIDELITY at 7 for a wave in which zero Protocol A pairs ran, so a tree targeting >= 7.0 that never runs it is capped at exactly its own bar.

amendments.finding: The primary human read was a newly invented ladder, duplicating RI-VIS06 Protocol A and resting on a stale claim that refs/modern/ is empty.
amendments.fix: Bind the primary read to RI-VIS06 Protocol A by path, paired blind against profile-matched plates from refs/modern/. Absolute Craft >= 7.0 rows in D, E and G read as their Protocol A equivalent. Delta rows (Craft >= pre-X + 1.5 on the minimum) survive unchanged - a same-pack comparison needs no external anchor. The owner's 'would you send this screenshot' question is retained and reported as a yes-rate, and is explicitly not a gate. Planted tell, pack quarantine, build/judge separation and census sample all kept as written. W1-30V's first action is to confirm the refs/modern/ citation routing, whether the acquired frames are HUD-free, and their licence position, since RI-VIS09 section 2 predates the acquisition; if it does not extend, that goes to ARBITRATION.md, not to a critic's local call.
amendments.overturned_by: an arbiter ruling that the acquired refs/modern/ folders may not be cited by the fidelity side, in which case the FIDELITY cap of 7 binds and the tree cannot demonstrate above 7.0 - which is a finding to report, not a reason to substitute an unanchored score

amendments.finding: The omitted concept-art child. The previous reviewer flagged that E and F may not cohere without one, declined it because it could not establish we can draw or license key art, and wrote that a reviewer adding it would be right.
amendments.fix: Ruled in as W1-30K, dispatchable now, blocking nothing. It draws nothing and licenses nothing: it derives a NUMERIC look target - per-region and per-settlement hue/value/chroma ranges, key-to-fill ratio, horizon visibility distance and fog density, silhouette and landform verbs, wear vocabulary - from plates already in the repo and already permitted, namely refs/morrowind/REF-A* for exactly the uses RI-VIS09 section 3.3 grants (palette, silhouette, built form, flora and creature design language), refs/anti-generic/ as negative anchor, refs/context/ as context only, refs/modern/ per profile for value and depth. Ships as two declared disjoint halves so RI-VIS01's CC-3 cross-citation sin cannot occur. Emits board.json so a critic checks a frame against a range rather than a paragraph. Owner is a new child, not W1-30V, because an agent must not author a target it also judges.
amendments.overturned_by: W1-30K finding that the plates cannot honestly ground the numbers, in which case its correct output is a short document saying so plus what acquisition would fix it

amendments.finding: Evidence over-testing and an unexecutable standard. (a) Every child's critic was told to run the full Deck - 288 stills + 12 sequences x >=180 frames = 2,448 frames - eleven times over for children that changed disjoint files, ~22,000 frames of duplicated capture, while W1-30V's own plan already defines child-scoped and smoke profiles nobody used. (b) The 144-frame orbit was required for every creature class, for a defect observed on one subject. (c) EVIDENCE section 4 bars SwiftShader from every appearance claim while every frame available today is SwiftShader and the GPU transport is unproven and may fail - as written, a transport failure stalls every child behind a gate none can run, which rule 0 forbids.
amendments.fix: (a) Child critics run child-scoped + the 12-shot unseen census sample + the complete open inventory; the full Deck runs once, at the parent's integration critic, at one stamped commit. The bar does not move. (b) Full 144-frame orbit for the player and any subject with an open inventory defect; 24 frames for other creature classes, escalating to full the moment any automatic check trips. (c) A named reversible SwiftShader fallback: delta and paired rows stand as full evidence; Protocol A results are recorded as a floor not an estimate, because our software frame is paired against a native capture of a shipped game; MSAA sample quality, anisotropic filtering and every absolute frame-time and draw-call budget stay CARRIED until one native run exists, and no child may be build-satisfied with a CARRIED budget row quietly closed.
amendments.overturned_by: the GPU transport landing, at which point (c) lapses; or SwiftShader and native disagreeing on a DELTA rather than an absolute, which invalidates the first bullet and is the first thing to check on the first native run

amendments.finding: The ownership table had a file claimed three times and two wrong seams. game/vendor/three/addons/** is claimed EXCLUSIVE by A while C vendors KTX2Loader and D vendors GLTFLoader, DRACOLoader and KTX2Loader - one area claimed three times, one file claimed twice. A's item 5 registers GRADE recipes into lighting-recipes.js, which B owns exclusively and which LIBRARY.md defines as LIGHT RIGS. The parent's table omitted render/lib/*.js, render/rig-contract.js, render/MATERIAL_API.md, world/noise.js and game/vendor/** although children claim them. The roads-and-boardwalks defect had two owners. The diagram idles G behind all of B and mis-orders H.
amendments.fix: vendor/ is additive-only and owned per file: A vendors the post-processing addons, D vendors the loaders, C may vendor KTX2Loader.js alone if its phase 2 needs it first; two vendorings of one addon or any edit to a vendored file are hard fails. Grade recipes move to render/post/grade-recipes.js, A's own file, keyed by the regionId/weatherId/timeOfDay B already publishes. The parent's table is completed. F closes the roads defect, E supplies the kit parts. G waits on B item 1 (the probe generator) not all of B; H does items 2,4,5,6,8 first and re-tunes after A and B.
amendments.overturned_by: a builder demonstrating that per-file vendor ownership cannot work because an addon genuinely needs a same-version patch, which would be a seam ruling not a local edit

amendments.finding: Cross-child acceptance rows had no named evaluation point. C's 'wear reads' is measured across E's kit parts and its styleboard-floor row uses the 8 settlement street shots, while C is building NOW and E has not started; A's grade row needs B's region identity; H's re-tune rows need A and B; G's dressing gates need E's kit. Unstated, this either blocks a child on a sibling or lets the row be quietly dropped.
amendments.fix: Such a row is marked DEFERRED in the child's verdict, naming the sibling it waits on, and is evaluated at the parent's integration critic. A deferred row is not a passed row; the integration critic's checklist is the union of every deferred row in the tree and the parent cannot close with one unevaluated.
amendments.overturned_by: nothing expected; this is bookkeeping that makes an existing structural intention explicit

amendments.finding: Boundary statement, so the next reviewer can see what was not touched.
amendments.fix: Unchanged: the demotion of M1-M12 to a tripwire, minimum-over-shots, the mandatory motion and orbit gates, the hard fail on stills-only evidence, the unseen census sample, the planted tell, the standing defect inventory and its three-angle closure rule, the library census and its two-consumer rule, the hard fails, the two 7.0 axis gates, the decomposition by file ownership, the seam commit and its byte-identical frame hash, and the ruling that children dispatch without waiting for the parent.

four_questions_asked_of_this_round.would_a_passing_build_look_good: Closer to yes after R1, and not fully. Applying PLAN-LOOP rule 3's own test: as written before this round, a competent builder could have got every check green while the load-bearing human gate was an unanchored agent opinion, which is the same class of failure as the noise-raisable statistics it replaced. After R1 the fidelity read is a blind paired comparison against a shipped game, which noise cannot win and which has a defined ladder and a defined cap. What remains genuinely uncertain, and is stated in the parent rather than papered over: whether naive agent judges are reproducible enough at the volume this standard implies. W1-30V's own falsification audit already names that and its fallback - fewer, better-anchored judgements on the minimum-scoring shots - is the right one.
four_questions_asked_of_this_round.concept_art_child: Ruled in as W1-30K. See R2. The previous reviewer's stop condition was the wrong question: not 'can we obtain key art' but 'can art direction be written down in a form a builder can hit and a critic can check'. Numbers can be; the prose style boards in world-art.js demonstrably have not been.
four_questions_asked_of_this_round.evidence_standard_cost: Over-testing on two axes and unexecutable on a third. See R3. The 288-still Deck is defensible as the parent's integration gate and indefensible eleven times over; the orbit ladder preserves the guard where the defect lives at a fifth of the frames; and the SwiftShader fallback keeps the standard runnable if the GPU transport fails. None of the three lowers the bar.
four_questions_asked_of_this_round.decomposition_safety: One area claimed three times (game/vendor/three/addons/**), one file claimed twice (KTX2Loader), one registry written by a non-owner (grade recipes into B's lighting-recipes.js), five paths claimed by children and missing from the parent's collision table, one defect with two owners, and two sequencing over-constraints. All repaired in R4. The C-phase-1 queue that D, E and F wait behind is real but cheap: C phase 1 depends on nothing, is already building, and MATERIAL_API.md is in progress.

orchestration/status/GPU-TRANSPORT-20260814.md: job 1 landed (ownership-scoped cleanup), job 2 in progress - SSH abandoned because the agent proxy re-terminates TLS, an HTTPS control agent on proxy.runpod.net being stood up. Unproven at the time of this review.
not_done: Did not run the game, did not open a browser, did not touch game/. Text only, as instructed.

Did not edit the nine satisfied child plans. Editing them would reset their plan states and disrupt S, C and V which are building now. The amendments live in the parent and in W1-30-EVIDENCE.md - the shared standard every child links and which carries no Plan-State of its own - and the parent states explicitly that an amendment overrides conflicting child text. The residual risk is real and named: a builder reads its child plan first, and a builder that never opens the parent will follow the superseded text. The mitigation available to the orchestrator is to hand the amendment list to each child's builder and critic in the dispatch brief.

Did not verify that the acquired refs/modern/ frames are HUD-free. The acquisition note records that HUD, cutscene and menu material was deliberately kept, and RI-VIS09 bars refs/modern/hud/ from ever appearing on the ref side of a blind pair. Whether individual frames in exterior_daylight and the other new folders carry HUD is unchecked, and it matters to R1's pairing. Named as W1-30V's job alongside the routing confirmation.

Did not verify the licence position of the acquired Steam-sourced reference frames; MANIFEST.json records licence: null on the exterior_daylight records I sampled. RI-VIS09's LICENCE-NOTE governs and this review did not read it against the new folders. Folded into V's routing confirmation.

Did not re-derive the ten code-level defects in Part 1 or the frame-level findings in Part 5b. They were spot-plausible and are not what this round was asked to test; the previous review's own status file records them with file and line.

Did not audit the other 25 plans for the same instruments-not-pictures defect. Directive section 2 says to assume the failure mode is not confined to graphics, and the previous review proposed it as a separate cheap piece. It remains unproposed to anyone and remains, in my judgement, the highest-value cheap piece available in the tree - the W1-30 diagnosis generalises and nobody has applied it anywhere else.

Did not resolve whether naive agent judges are reproducible at the volume this standard implies. It is W1-30V's declared least-certain item and it is the largest remaining risk to the primary gate after R1.

Lost roughly forty minutes to git contention: a concurrent agent's merge wiped this review's working-tree edits and new files entirely (git gc plus several commits held .git/index.lock for minutes, then a merge reverted the tree). All edits were reconstructed from context and re-applied, with copies kept outside the repo. Nothing was lost, but any agent editing orchestration/ during a heavy window should keep a scratchpad copy before it starts.
